questions.question_text:
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 58$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 9$.
What is the raw value with a $z$-score of $1.4$?

options.why: Subtracted $z\sigma$ from the mean even though $z$ is positive, placing the value below the mean.
Stopped at $z\sigma = 1.4 \times 9$ and forgot to add the mean.
Added the z-score itself to the mean instead of multiplying it by the standard deviation first.

questions.question_text:
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 210$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 16$.
What is the raw value with a $z$-score of $-0.75$?

options.why: Ignored the negative sign on $z$ and added $12$ instead of subtracting it.
Added the $z$-score itself to the mean, $210+(-0.75)$, instead of multiplying it by the standard deviation first.
Subtracted a whole standard deviation, treating any negative z-score as one deviation below the mean.

questions.question_text:
The marks in an examination have a mean of $64$ and a standard deviation of $7$.
What mark is $2.5$ standard deviations below the mean?

options.why: Added instead of subtracting, giving the mark $2.5$ standard deviations above the mean.
Subtracted $2.5$ from the mean instead of $2.5$ standard deviations.
Subtracted a single standard deviation, ignoring the factor of $2.5$.

questions.solution_text:
$2.5$ standard deviations below the mean means $z = -2.5$.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 64 + (-2.5) \times 7$
$= 64 - 17.5$
$= 46.5$

questions.question_text:
A test has a mean mark of $54$ and a standard deviation of $6.4$.
What mark corresponds to a $z$-score of $-1.25$?

options.why: Ignored the negative sign on the z-score and added $1.25\times6.4=8$ to the mean.
Subtracted $1.25$ from the mean instead of multiplying it by the standard deviation first.
Subtracted one standard deviation, $6.4$, instead of $1.25$ standard deviations.

questions.question_text:
A reading test has a mean mark of $62.5$ and a standard deviation of $5.2$.
What mark corresponds to a standardised score of $2.25$?

options.why: Subtracted $2.25\times5.2=11.7$ from the mean even though the z-score is positive.
Added the z-score to the mean without multiplying it by the standard deviation.
Calculated $z\sigma$ but forgot to add the mean.

questions.question_text:
A fitness test has a mean mark of $73.6$ and a standard deviation of $4.8$.
What mark is $1.75$ standard deviations below the mean?

options.why: Added $1.75$ standard deviations, finding a mark above the mean instead of below it.
Subtracted $1.75$ from the mean instead of $1.75$ standard deviations.
Subtracted only one standard deviation, ignoring the factor of $1.75$.

questions.solution_text:
$1.75$ standard deviations below the mean means $z = -1.75$.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 73.6 + (-1.75) \times 4.8$
$= 73.6 - 8.4$
$= 65.2$
